info.title: picgen API
info.description: The HTTP API behind picgen studio. Everything the studio page does goes through these endpoints. JSON in and out, except uploads (multipart) and images (PNG). Errors are JSON `{"error": "..."}` with a 4xx or 5xx status. There is no authentication in v1.0: run picgen on a private network or behind an authenticating reverse proxy.

post.summary: Magic erase: remove what is under a mask and fill in the background
post.description: Like a phone's magic eraser. Send a picture and a mask (white = erase, black = keep); the masked pixels are replaced by Qwen-Image-Edit's reconstruction of the background and **every pixel outside the mask is returned unchanged**. Runs synchronously on the GPU (about a minute; the request blocks). Optional `prompt` hints at what is behind the object ("the wooden desk and the chalkboard"); `feather` (px, default 6) softens the seam; `seed` makes it repeatable. Used by the GIMP plug-in *Filters → Faraway → Magic Erase*, which sends the current selection as the mask.

mask.description: PNG, same size as the image (resized if not); white = erase.

prompt.description: What is behind the erased thing (optional).

post.description:
Adds a job to the queue and returns its id at once. The **model's mode** decides what kind of picture it is:

| Mode | Needs | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `txt2img` | `prompt` | `{"prompt": "a lighthouse at dusk", "model": "z-image-turbo"}` |
| `character` | `prompt`, `characters` | `{"prompt": "runs away scared", "model": "flux-kontext", "characters": ["c1791012478462"]}` |
| `edit` | `prompt`, `edit_of` | `{"prompt": "make it night", "model": "flux-kontext-edit", "edit_of": "1791022789-4284"}` |

Characters are ignored by `txt2img` models, so pass a `character`-mode model when you pass a character. `qwen-image` / `qwen-image-edit` are the commercially licensed character and edit models; both accept `extra_refs` (up to two more pictures, for a second character or a prop) and keep 8 steps / cfg 1 whatever you pass. Steps are clamped to 1–60 and guidance to 0–15. Leave them out to let picgen choose (it raises them when pose or face guides are used on the FLUX models).

prompt.description: What to draw (or, for edits, what to change). Up to 2000 characters.

model.description: Image model id from `/api/image_models`. Default: the server default.

seed.description: Seed for repeatable results. Default: random.

characters.description: Character ids (at most `max_characters`, currently 1). Character mode only.

character.description: Deprecated single-character form of `characters`; when present it replaces the list.

reference.description: Identity/pose reference: `auto` (planner decides), `original`, an own view tag, or `lib:<tag>`.

garments.description: `"auto"` (wear what the prompt names) or a list of library tags (at most `max_garments`; `[]` for none).

edit_of.description: Edit mode: the picture to change, as a picture id or `char:<character id>[:<view tag>]`.

guides.description: Character mode: `false` skips the planner's pose/expression library guides and uses only the identity reference (plus `extra_refs`). Use with `qwen-image`, which treats every reference as a character to draw.

loras.description: Up to three LoRA files from `models/loras` (`z-image-turbo` only), each as a file name or `{name, strength}` (strength 0–2, default 1). Put each LoRA's trigger word in the prompt. Unknown files are dropped.

extra_refs.description: Up to two further reference pictures (picture ids or `char:<cid>[:<view>]`) appended after the planner's references: a second character, a prop. Character and edit modes; `qwen-image` sees up to three pictures in all.

feedback_id.description: Feedback row the fix or retry answers.

patch.summary: Switch a lesson on or off, or change it
patch.description: Allowed fields: `enabled`, `title`, `why`, `trigger` (an object such as `{"when": "keywords", "any": ["waving"]}`, or simply a list or comma-separated string of keywords), `action` (an object). Numbers are clamped: `guidance_min`/`guidance_max` 1–10, `steps_min` 4–60; values that are not numbers are dropped. Editing a built-in lesson's text, trigger or action marks it as edited, so the change survives restarts. Switching a lesson off sets `owner_off`, so the automatic check never switches it back on.

ref.description: `original`, an own view tag, or `lib:<tag>` for a library item.

mode.description: `original`, `own` (this character's own picture), `guide` (another character's picture) or `edit`.

why.description: Why it was chosen: `keywords`, `picked by hand`, the matched words, or `repair guide`.

pose.description: Body pose or activity reference, if any.

garments.description: Garments to wear (at most `max_garments`, and only while references remain).

notes.description: Warnings, e.g. garments dropped for lack of reference slots.

ref_count.description: References the picture will use (1–4). Each beyond the first adds about 55 s.

boost.description: A pose or face guide is in play, so guidance and steps are raised if you left them at the defaults.

guidance.description: Guidance that will actually be used, after boost and lessons.

steps.description: Steps that will actually be used.

lesson_notes.description: What those lessons changed in the plan.

prompt_preview.description: The prompt after lessons, before reference wording is added.

seconds.description: Rough time estimate on the reference GPU.

file.description: PNG file name; fetch it from `/img/<file>`.

reference_used.description: Identity reference (`original`, a view tag or `lib:<tag>`).

lessons_applied.description: Keys of lessons that changed this picture.

prompt_sent.description: The exact text the model received.

edit_of.description: Source picture id, or `char:<cid>[:<tag>]`, for edits.

extra_refs.description: Further reference pictures passed with the request.

outcome.description: For fixes/retries: which flagged flaws `cleared`, `remaining` or were `introduced`.

guide_used.description: Pose picture used to steer a guided fix.

feedback.description: Gallery only: the latest grade `{feedback_id, verdict, issues, fix_image_id, at}`.

Job.description: A job. While queued or running it is the live job record; once done it is the full `Picture` record plus `status` and `file`.

source.description: `generated` (sheet), `uploaded`, `derived` (drawn from a library item) or `taught` (an approved picture saved with `POST /api/feedback/teach`).

kind.description: `expression`, `pose` or `activity`, or a garment kind for derived views.

species.description: What it is (`woman`, `dog`, `robot`…); used in prompts.

from_image.description: Gallery picture it was made from, if any.

views.description: Every view by tag. Fetch a view from `/char/<id>/sheet/<file>`.

sheet_wanted.description: Sheet tags this character should have.

tag.description: Unique id; use `lib:<tag>` as a reference.

keywords.description: Words the planner matches. Several words = a phrase. A leading `!` marks a weak garment word that can rank but not qualify an item.

source.description: Character drawn in it (its identity for that character, a guide for others), `""` for generic, or `synthesized`.

views.description: Panels in the picture (3 for front/side/back composites).

error.description: Present instead of the fields above when the check could not run.

Critique.description: What the vision model saw, compared with the request.

prompt.description: Edit instruction that changes only the flagged things. You may reword it.

strategy.description: `fix` (words only) or `guided` (also steered by a pose picture).

guide.description: `{tag, label, drawn:false}` (library pose) or `{synthesize, label, drawn:true}` (drawn first).

regenerate.description: A fresh-picture alternative; submit it to `POST /api/generate` with `feedback_id`.

keeps.description: What the fix is told to keep: the character's permanent features (read once from its reference picture), and the picture's clothing, held objects and setting.

Repair.description: A ready-to-submit `POST /api/generate` body that fixes a flagged picture.

when.description: `always`, `character`, `keywords` (with `any`), or a built-in condition such as `gaze_phrase`.

action.description: What it changes. Built-ins can also use structural actions (`gaze_expand`, `expr_expand`, `identity_original`, `drop_guides_for_garments`).

source.description: `builtin`, `user` or `ai` (proposed by the learner; starts off).

user_edited.description: 1 when you changed a built-in's text, trigger or action; it is then kept across restarts.

owner_off.description: 1 when you switched it off; the automatic check will not switch it back on.

Lesson.description: A rule applied before drawing when its trigger matches.
